title: Born Into Opportunity: How Childhood Environment Shapes the American Dream
text:
To what extent does the socioeconomic environment someone grows up in influence their future income, financial stability, and opportunities in adulthood?

Using data from the Opportunity Atlas, we track millions of U.S. children from childhood into adulthood to test whether two children born into equally low-income families (at the 25th income percentile, around $27,000/year) end up with dramatically different financial futures simply because of where they grew up.

title: Born Into Opportunity: How Childhood Environment Shapes the American Dream
section: Interactive Map: Where Does the American Dream Thrive?
text:
Interactive Map: Where Does the American Dream Thrive?
This map shows the average adult household income percentile of children who grew up in low-income families (25th percentile) in each U.S. county. Deep teal and blue areas offer the strongest upward mobility, while warm coral and orange areas show places where children from low-income families struggle most to climb the income ladder. Zoom in and hover over any county to explore!

title: Born Into Opportunity: How Childhood Environment Shapes the American Dream
section: 1. Neighborhood Environment: Does Growing Up in a Wealthier Area Boost Adult Earnings?
text:
1. Neighborhood Environment: Does Growing Up in a Wealthier Area Boost Adult Earnings?
Every point below is a U.S. county (with at least 500 low-income children). Even though all of these children started in families at the 25th income percentile, growing up in a county with higher household income and lower poverty is strongly linked to higher adult earnings.
